column1: charisma§Charisma explains the crowd, not the policy.§**魅力**能解释人群，解释不了政策。
charitable§The trust is charitable in law and commercial in habit.§这个信托在法律上是**慈善的**，在做法上是商业的。
charlatan§Every new field attracts a charlatan or two.§每个新兴领域都会招来一两个**骗子**。
cheapen§Do not cheapen a real apology by attaching conditions.§不要给真诚的道歉附加条件，那会让它**变得廉价**。
cheerfully§He cheerfully admitted he had never read the book.§他**爽快**地承认自己从没读过那本书。
cherish§The town cherishes a story that the records do not support.§这个镇**珍视**一个记录并不支持的故事。
chicanery§The chicanery lay in the footnotes, not the headline.§**狡辩**藏在脚注里，而不在标题上。
chide§The editor chided herself for missing an obvious date.§编辑**责怪**自己漏掉了一个明显的日期。
chronicle§Her letters chronicle the slow arrival of electricity.§她的信件**记录**了电力缓慢到来的过程。
churlish§A churlish refusal is remembered longer than a generous yes.§**粗鲁**的拒绝比慷慨的答应被记得更久。
circuitous§His reasoning is circuitous and lands somewhere sensible.§他的推理**绕来绕去**，最后落到一个合理的地方。
circumlocution§Bureaucratic circumlocution adds a week to every request.§官僚式的**绕圈子**给每项申请都增加一周。
circumscribe§Illness circumscribed his travel but not his correspondence.§疾病**限制**了他的出行，却没限制他的通信。
circumspect§Be circumspect about numbers you cannot trace to a source.§对追溯不到来源的数字要保持**谨慎**。
circumspection§A little circumspection would have saved the whole quarter.§稍微**谨慎**一点就能保住整个季度。
circumvent§Water circumvents an obstacle rather than arguing with it.§水会**绕开**障碍，而不是与它争辩。
clairvoyant§You do not need to be clairvoyant to see how this ends.§不用有**透视**眼也看得出这事会怎么收场。
clandestine§A clandestine copy of the report reached the press first.§报告的一份**秘密**副本先一步到了媒体手里。
clarity§Clarity costs the writer time and saves the reader more.§**清晰**让作者多花时间，却为读者省下更多。
cleanse§He cleansed the wound and left the dressing to the nurse.§他**清洗**了伤口，包扎交给护士。
clientele§A quiet clientele of scholars kept the shop alive.§一批安静的学者**客户**让这家店活了下来。
clinical§The trial is clinical, not laboratory, and takes four years.§这是**临床**试验而非实验室试验，需要四年。
cloy§Praise cloys when it arrives every day.§每天都来的赞美会让人**腻**烦。
clumsily§The joint was clumsily repaired and held for thirty years.§这个接头修得很**粗糙**，却撑了三十年。
clutter§Clear the clutter and the room turns out to be large.§清掉**杂物**，才发现房间其实很大。
coalesce§Droplets coalesce on the glass and then run down.§水珠在玻璃上**聚合**，然后流下。
coalition§A coalition of tenants and shopkeepers stopped the demolition.§一个由租户和店主组成的**联盟**阻止了拆除。
coddle§An engine that is coddled in winter lasts longer.§冬天被**细心呵护**的发动机寿命更长。
coerce§Evidence obtained under coercion was struck from the record.§在**胁迫**下取得的证据被从记录中剔除。
cogent§The most cogent objection came from a first-year student.§最**有说服力的**反对意见来自一位一年级学生。
cognition§Damage to that area affects cognition but not movement.§该区域受损影响**认知**，但不影响运动。
cognizant§I am cognizant of the cost and I still recommend it.§我**清楚**这笔花费，仍然建议这么做。
coherent§Three coherent paragraphs beat ten brilliant sentences.§三个**条理清楚**的段落胜过十个精彩的句子。
cohesive§The mortar is cohesive enough to hold without reinforcement.§这种砂浆**黏性**足够，不加钢筋也能固定。
collaborator§A wartime collaborator, he was tried and then quietly employed.§作为战时的**合作者**，他受审后又被悄悄雇用。
collage§Memory works by collage rather than by film.§记忆的运作方式像**拼贴**，而不像电影。
colloquially§Colloquially the building is the Cathedral; officially it is Store Four.§**口语里**这栋楼叫“大教堂”，官方名称是四号仓库。
combat§He saw combat for eleven days and wrote about it for fifty years.§他经历了十一天**战斗**，写了五十年。
comical§There is something comical about a warning nobody can read.§一条没人看得懂的警告本身就有点**滑稽**。
commandeer§She commandeered the only table with a lamp.§她**占下**了唯一一张带台灯的桌子。
commemorate§The date is commemorated by a half-day closure and nothing else.§这个日子只以半天闭馆来**纪念**，别无其他。
commend§I commend the appendix to anyone who doubts the conclusion.§凡是怀疑这个结论的人，我都**推荐**去看附录。
commendable§A commendable failure teaches more than a lucky success.§**值得称道**的失败比侥幸的成功教人更多。
commendation§The commendation was framed and hung in the wrong corridor.§那份**嘉奖**被裱起来，却挂错了走廊。
commiseration§They exchanged commiseration about the weather and got to work.§他们互相**同情**了几句天气，然后开始干活。
commodity§Attention has become the commodity everyone is selling.§注意力已成为人人都在贩卖的**商品**。
commonness§The commonness of the plant hid how quickly it was vanishing.§这种植物的**常见**掩盖了它消失的速度。
commonplace§It is a commonplace of the field and still not true.§这是这个领域里的**老生常谈**，却依然不对。
community§A research community can be smaller than a village.§一个研究**共同体**可能比一个村子还小。
comparability§Comparability across years broke when the method changed.§方法一变，跨年度的**可比性**就断了。
comparable§There is no comparable collection outside two capitals.§除了两个首都，别处没有**可与之相比**的收藏。
compassionate§He was granted compassionate leave and never came back.§他获准了**恩恤假**，之后再没回来。
compatibility§Compatibility with the old format was abandoned in version three.§第三版放弃了与旧格式的**兼容**。
compatible§Her account is compatible with the photographs, if not with his.§她的说法与照片**相符**，尽管与他的说法不符。
compel§Curiosity, not duty, compelled him to open the box.§**让他打开箱子的**是好奇，不是义务。
compendious§A compendious footnote can be worth a chapter.§一条**简明的**脚注可能抵得上一章。
competitive§She is competitive about everything except her own work.§除了自己的工作，她对什么都**好胜**。
complacent§Nobody is complacent after a summer like that one.§经历了那样一个夏天，没人还会**自满**。
complain§He complained in writing, which is why anything changed.§他是**书面投诉**的，所以事情才有了改变。
complement§Two hundred is the ship's full complement.§两百人是这艘船的**满员编制**。
complexity§Complexity is not depth, though it is often mistaken for it.§**复杂**不等于深刻，尽管常被误认为如此。
compliant§The building is compliant with a code that was rewritten last year.§这栋楼**符合**去年重写过的规范。
complicity§Complicity requires knowledge, which is why the emails mattered.§**共谋**需要知情，这正是那些邮件要紧的原因。
complimentary§Tickets were complimentary, which explains the full house.§票是**赠送**的，这就解释了为何满座。
compound§Interest compounds quietly and then all at once.§利息先是悄悄**累积**，随后一下子爆发。
comprehend§A child can comprehend the rule long before she can state it.§孩子早在能说出规则之前就已经**理解**它了。
comprehensible§Make it comprehensible first and elegant second.§先让它**易懂**，其次才是优雅。
